title: Customer Loyalty Program Ideas: Successful Program Examples
summary: As you develop your own customer loyalty program ideas, learn what makes a loyalty program work, and get inspiration from major ecommerce brands.
body_markdown:
A customer loyalty program is a structured reward system that lets customers earn credits and benefits for making purchases and engaging with your business. Customers give you repeat business and their contact information, and you reward them with savings, access, or status.


According to the[Global Customer Loyalty Report 2026](https://antavo.com/blog/global-customer-loyalty-report-2026/) from loyalty platform Antavo, 90% of program owners who measure performance reported positive[return on investment (ROI)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/what-is-return-on-investment) , at an average of 5.3 times. Nearly as many (89.4%) said their loyalty program delivers value they wouldn’t capture otherwise.


Here’s what loyalty programs are, why they’re valuable, and which features make them succeed, plus ideas and guidance for building one of your own with Shopify apps and automation tools.


## What are customer loyalty programs?


[Customer loyalty programs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/loyalty-program) are marketing programs that reward engaged or repeat customers and encourage long-term relationships with your brand. Loyalty program members might receive a birthday gift or discount, or earn rewards for actions like making purchases, referring new customers, or following the business on social media. Some programs give points that can be used toward purchases; others sort customers into tiers by spending milestones, with better benefits at each level.


By improving[retention](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-retention-retail) and raising repeat purchase rates, loyalty programs aim to grow[customer lifetime value (CLV)](https://www.shopify.com/blog/customer-lifetime-value) . In[an analysis of more than 205 million orders across 3,000 brands](https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250501427280/en/Your-Loyalty-Program-Is-Your-Insurance-Policy-Redeeming-Loyalty-Program-Members-Are-4X-More-Likely-to-Repeat-Purchase-When-Consumer-Confidence-Slumps) , loyalty platform LoyaltyLion found that 88% of members who redeem rewards go on to buy again, compared with roughly 28% of non-members.


Loyalty programs also generate[first-party data](https://www.shopify.com/enterprise/blog/first-party-data) from purchasing behavior and preferences, which you can feed back into personalized rewards. Customers can join using their email address, phone number, or a profile login created after their first purchase. From there, you can use customer profiles to track buying and browsing habits to tailor rewards to individual tastes.


For example, if you sell coffee beans and a member keeps buying the same blend, you could offer a discount on their next bag, or invite them to sample a roast with a similar flavor profile before it launches.


## Customer loyalty program ideas


There are several[types of customer loyalty programs](https://www.shopify.com/blog/loyalty-program) , each structured to give customers a clear, easy path to earning rewards. The main structures are:


-


**Points-based.** Customers earn points for purchases and other actions (referring friends, or promoting your business on social media) and then redeem them for rewards like free shipping, discounts, or store credit.


-


**Tiered.** Customers are grouped by how much they spend, moving into higher tiers with increasingly exclusive perks as they hit new spending marks. For example, base-tier customers might get a standing discount, while VIP customers get that plus priority support.


-


**Paid.** Customers pay to join (an annual membership fee or a recurring subscription) in exchange for benefits like free shipping, lower prices, or extended warranty coverage.


-


**Value-based.** Instead of direct rewards, you tie purchases to a cause, retaining customers by appealing to shared values rather than discounts.


-


**Hybrid.** A combination of two or more of the above. For example, a points program that sorts members into tiers based on the points they’ve accrued.


## What makes a customer loyalty program idea successful?


Drawing on findings from loyalty software brand[Antavo](https://apps.shopify.com/antavo-loyalty-cloud-prod) ’s[Global Customer Loyalty Report 2026](https://adindex.ru/publication/analitics/search/342713/img/Global_Customer_Loyalty_Report_2026_by_Antavo.pdf) and the[2026 EY Loyalty Market Study](https://www.ey.com/content/dam/ey-unified-site/ey-com/en-us/campaigns/cmo/documents/loyalty-study-report-final.pdf) , here are some of the most important qualities consumers look for in a loyalty program:


-


**Attainable rewards.** Give customers clear information on exactly how to earn rewards. If being rewarded takes too long or is too difficult, customers may lose interest.


-


**Monetary savings.** Customers want their participation in loyalty programs to help them save money on purchases.


-


**Free products and services.** You can also offer customers savings on shipping, along with bonus products and free samples. You can deepen the experience further with perks like complimentary repairs and maintenance.


-


**Personalization.** Consumers want loyalty programs that feel catered to their needs and preferences. Show members you’re tuned in to their tastes by acting on what their data already tells you, recommending products based on past purchases, sending a reward for a category they browse often, or timing an offer to when they usually reorder.


-


**Priority treatment.** Think events, exclusive access to sales and product launches, and preferential customer service treatment. These kinds of perks can make loyalty members feel special, like they’re getting an exceptional customer experience in exchange for their support.


-


**Ease of use.** Successful loyalty programs are straightforward and user-friendly. Their structure should be easy to follow, rewards should feel attainable, and the benefits customers earn should feel worth the effort it took to get them.

## Customer loyalty program examples for inspiration


- Ouai
- Duvin
- Years
- Jaxon Lane
- Manscaped


These brands have designed loyalty programs using the structures above, in different combinations:


### Ouai


Source:[Ouai](https://theouai.com/pages/ouai-obsessed) .


Beauty brand[Ouai](https://theouai.com/) rewards customers through a[points-based loyalty program](https://www.shopify.com/blog/points-programs) called[Ouai Obsessed](https://theouai.com/pages/ouai-obsessed) . On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/ouai-creative-copy-that-engages-customers) , former CEO Hannah Beals describes the program as “finding different ways to reward your customer for their interactions like leaving a comment, providing product feedback, being a repeat purchaser, or wearing your merch on Instagram.” Members earn points—called coins—for those actions and put them toward purchases.


But points are only part of it. Working with loyalty platform[TYB](https://www.tyb.xyz/) , Ouai built the program around experiences and participatory challenges. According to[TYB](https://www.tyb.xyz/case-studies/ouai-unifies-loyalty-rewards-and-community----driving-65-higher-ltv-with-tyb) , Obsessed members show 65% higher lifetime value than nonmembers.


Hannah also notes the brand uses purchase data to give superfans early access to product drops: “We’ve handpicked everyone on our website who has bought something in that fragrance already,” she says, “and we’re gonna do something personalized and high touch for all the customers that we know love the scent.”


### Duvin


Source:[Duvin](https://duvindesign.com/pages/souvenir-shop) .


Beach-inspired leisurewear brand[Duvin](https://duvindesign.com/) runs a tiered program called[The Souvenir Shop](https://duvindesign.com/pages/souvenir-shop) , granting reward levels based on how much customers spend. All three tiers—Social Membership (Free), Full Resort Access ($250 minimum), and VIP ($750 minimum)—include a points multiplier, a birthday reward, and early access to new product releases. The top two add richer perks: higher multipliers, larger birthday rewards, free shipping, and secret product access.


By scaling both the value and the exclusivity of each tier, Duvin gives customers a reason to climb. At its prices, a customer needs to buy around five items a year to reach Full Resort Access and 13 to make VIP, so the first promotion feels attainable, while VIP status shows a genuine commitment to the brand.


### Years


Source:[Years](https://yearsbeer.com/pages/leisure-society-club) .


Non-alcoholic beer brand[Years](https://yearsbeer.com/) has a paid loyalty program, the[Society of Leisure](https://yearsbeer.com/pages/leisure-society-club) , that rewards members with free shipping, cheaper six-packs, early access to new beers and exclusive events, 20% off merch, and a free six-pack on their birthday. Membership costs $29 annually—roughly the cost of one six-pack, delivered. And instead of earning their way to rewards through accrued spend amounts, members unlock every perk the moment they sign up and pay.


For Years, the model works because the only physical product included with a membership is the birthday six-pack.


### Jaxon Lane


Source:[Jaxon Lane](https://jaxonlane.com/pages/rewards) .


Men’s skincare label[Jaxon Lane](https://jaxonlane.com/) uses a hybrid program to build loyalty and encourage repeat purchases. Its[rewards program](https://jaxonlane.com/pages/rewards) lets customers earn points for purchases and non-transactional actions like subscribing to the brand’s email and SMS list, following it on social media, referring friends, and leaving reviews. Points redeem for discounts or free products, while annual spend sorts customers into loyalty tiers.


Customer service is central to how Jaxon Lane builds retention against bigger retailers like Amazon. On[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/jaxon-lane-product-development-and-public-relations-tips) , cofounder Jen Yu says personal touches make loyal customers feel appreciated: “We have free shipping for frequent customers, we throw in surprise gifts, we write handwritten notes,” she says. “We do everything we can to help our customer be successful in their skincare journey and enjoy shopping with us.”


### Manscaped


Source:[Manscaped](https://www.manscaped.com/pages/members-only) .


To encourage repeat purchases of their men’s grooming products,[Manscaped](https://www.manscaped.com/) has a hybrid[rewards program](https://www.manscaped.com/pages/members-only) that combines points, tiers, and a subscription. Every customer joins the free Guest List, earning five points per dollar plus a birthday gift, with points redeemable as Rewards Cash—1,000 points converts to $10.


Spending $100 in a year promotes a customer to A-List, which bumps earning to eight points per dollar and adds a Manniversary gift—a special annual reward commemorating the day members joined the rewards program—and early access to new products. The top tier, VIP, is reached by subscribing to a VIP package, which unlocks 10 points per dollar, discounted pricing, extended warranty coverage, free samples, and an annual loyalty gift.


On Shopify Masters, Founder Paul Tran says that with so many benefits, it’s hard to pin down the program’s single[value proposition](https://www.shopify.com/blog/value-proposition) : “Having choice, collecting the rewards points, getting discounts, and extending your warranty, are all big parts of the appeal.”


## How to use Shopify-native loyalty program apps


There are several loyalty apps in the[Shopify App Store](https://apps.shopify.com/) , including[LoyaltyLion](https://apps.shopify.com/loyaltylion) ,[Smile](https://apps.shopify.com/smile-io) ,[Yotpo](https://apps.shopify.com/swell) ,[Rivo](https://apps.shopify.com/rivo-loyalty) , and[Growave](https://apps.shopify.com/growave) .


These apps integrate with[Shopify admin](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-admin) ,[Shopify Flow](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow) , and[Shopify POS](https://www.shopify.com/pos) to sync directly with your store.


Each can help you build a points-based, tiered, or hybrid program and reward customers for actions like referring friends or having a birthday, and each has a free version, with paid tiers that scale by order volume, so pricing tends to track your store’s size rather than a flat fee. You design the program that fits your business, and the platform handles the tedious parts: onboarding new members, tracking each customer’s point balance and spending tier, and reporting on how the program is performing.

## How to create a DIY loyalty program on Shopify


If it isn’t within your budget to start a loyalty program using one of the apps listed above, there are free Shopify tools you can use to design one from scratch.


On an episode of[Shopify Masters](https://www.shopify.com/blog/harlem-candle-co-scent-of-success) ,[Harlem Candle Company](https://www.harlemcandleco.com/) Founder Teri Johnson shares how she creates a loyalty experience without a formal app. After creating a segment of customers who consistently open her marketing emails and frequently make new purchases, Teri rewards those VIPs with early access to products.


“With email marketing it’s just amazing to be able to create segments and customer groups of who your VIPs are,” Teri says. “Those people who open up every email, add stuff to cart, and check out almost every time.”


You can take Teri’s approach and[create segments](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/customers/customer-segmentation/create-customer-segments#template) based on customer engagement, email open rate, or purchasing habits. You can also use Shopify to create customer profiles and segment customers using that information. From there, you can create your own tiered system, use a general VIP segment, or target customers who are fans of a specific product and grant them early access when it is about to be offered at a reduced price.


[Shopify Flow](https://apps.shopify.com/flow) is an automation tool that enables you to create[loyalty workflows](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/getting-started/workflow-examples#loyalty) using different triggers to spark actions. For example, you can reward a VIP customer on their birthday by setting up a date-based trigger to send an email a few days before their birthday with a discount code.


[Creating workflows](https://help.shopify.com/en/manual/shopify-flow/create) like this, using your customer segments, lets you set up a loyalty program without a third-party app.


## Customer loyalty program FAQ


### How do loyalty programs increase customer retention?


Loyalty programs increase customer retention by rewarding participants with exclusive discounts, special events, early access to new products and sales, priority treatment, and other benefits.


### What is the difference between a rewards program and a referral program?


A referral program is a specific type of rewards program. Referral programs are exclusively built around rewarding existing customers for referring new customers. Rewards programs may offer rewards for referring new customers, but rewards members can earn points and prizes for other actions like following a business on social media, making a purchase, or leaving a review.


### How do you measure loyalty program success?


Loyalty program success is often measured by three metrics:


1. **Return on investment (ROI).** Shows how much the program earns your business relative to what it costs to run.


2. **Average order value (AOV).** Tracks how much customers spend per order. Compare it against your pre-program AOV to see whether it’s risen.


3. **Customer lifetime value (CLV).** Estimates total spend across the whole customer relationship; measured before and after launch, it shows whether the program is deepening loyalty over time
